commitResults.messageTitle: Allow lessons to run past midnight
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson's end time had to be later than its start time, so a late
lesson such as Friday 2200 to 0100 could not be recorded.

Read an end time earlier than the start time as ending on the next
day, with the lesson belonging to the day it starts on. Only an end
time equal to the start time is still rejected. Swapped start and end
times are therefore no longer reported as a mistake.

Update the developer guide and the lesson model notes to match.

Closes #52. addlesson n/NAME d/DAY st/START_TIME et/END_TIME adds a
weekly lesson, and deletelesson INDEX deletes the lesson at that index
in the displayed lesson list, keeping its students.

A day is one of mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat or sun in any letter
case, and a time is exactly four digits from 0000 to 2359. The rules
for a lesson's name and times stay in Lesson, whose own messages are
shown. A duplicate lesson is rejected even when a filter hides it.

Tests also cover that deleting a lesson or a student removes only its
own enrolments, both in the model and in the saved file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for finding students by phone number
commitResults.messageBody:
findstudent will take p/ followed by digit sequences, matching students
whose own or guardian's phone number contains any of them. These tests
do not compile yet: the predicate has no phone keyword list and the
parser has no phone keyword error message.

A tutor often gets a call or message from a number they have not
saved, and needs to know which student or family it belongs to.

findstudent now takes p/ followed by digit sequences. It matches
students whose own or guardian's phone number contains any of them.
As with n/ and gn/, a student must match every prefix given.

Name keywords are now checked against the rule in Name instead of a
separate copy of it, so search stays in step if that rule changes.

and parsePhoneKeywords.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update Model and Storage class diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagrams were drawn before the lesson model was implemented. They
show classes that do not exist (TutorBook, UniqueStudentList,
UniqueLessonList, LessonName, EnrolmentList, JsonAdaptedGuardian) and
have each student hold its lessons.

Let's redraw them to match the code. AddressBook holds lists of
students, lessons and enrolments, and each Enrolment links a student
UUID to a lesson UUID. The storage side mirrors this with a
JsonAdaptedEnrolment list, and stores guardian details as fields of
JsonAdaptedStudent.
